home-remodeling.local_heading: A young city with dated interiors
intro_paragraphs: Parkland is a young city with an old temperament. Almost nothing here predates the 1970s, and the housing arrived in two distinct waves: acreage estates out in Pine Tree Estates and The Ranches, then the master-planned surge that produced Country Place, Cypress Head, Parkland Isles and Heron Bay through the 1990s and 2000s. Those production houses are large and structurally sound and thoroughly of their decade inside, with formal rooms nobody enters and bulkhead soffits ringed in recessed cans. Whole-home remodeling in Parkland is usually about editing a floor plan, not rescuing a ruin.

Permits are issued by the City of Parkland Building Department, which sits inside Development Services and takes submittals through the city's online permitting portal, with a current survey and signed and sealed plans in the package. Broward then adds a layer most homeowners never encounter directly: the county Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code across Broward, certifies the plans examiners and inspectors assigned to your job, and issues the formal interpretations that settle disputes. Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window and door carries HVHZ product approval. Your association's architectural committee is a wholly separate approval.

That claim rests on more than twenty years of South Florida construction and 150-plus delivered remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected. In Parkland that shows up as a scope written down and priced before the first wall opens, someone from our team on site every working day, floors and cabinetry protected in the half of the house that is not being touched, and crews who sign in at the guardhouse without incident. The same team carries the job from first estimate to warranty call, which means there is nobody to hand you off to.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing begins until the work is written down and priced. Here is what a whole-house project on this side of Broward usually includes.

scope_items.name: Killing the formal rooms
scope_items.desc: Removing the walls that isolate a living room nobody uses from the kitchen everyone stands in, with engineered beams and a load path carried to footing.

scope_items.name: Ceilings, soffits and light
scope_items.desc: Tearing out bulkhead soffits and the ring of cans around them, then rebuilding flat ceilings with layered lighting and mechanicals rerouted rather than boxed in.

scope_items.name: Impact glass, finally
scope_items.desc: Trading accordion shutters and original units for HVHZ-approved impact windows and doors, with product approvals filed where Broward inspectors expect to find them.

scope_items.name: Electrical and mechanical reset
scope_items.desc: New panels and circuits, air handlers and ductwork sized for the house as it will be, and plumbing corrected where the original builder took the shortest route.

scope_items.name: Flooring, millwork and stone
scope_items.desc: One continuous floor across the whole plan, millwork scaled to ten-foot ceilings, and slabs selected in the yard instead of chosen off a sample chart.

faqs.q: Who issues the building permit for a remodel in Parkland?
faqs.a: The City of Parkland Building Department, part of Development Services at City Hall on University Drive. Applications and drawings go up through the city's online permitting portal, and the submittal needs a survey less than a year old alongside signed and sealed plans. Standing behind the city is the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies the plans examiners and inspectors and maintains the county's code amendments. Filing and the inspection calendar are our job, not yours.

faqs.q: Does my HOA have to approve the work before the city does?
faqs.a: Practically, yes, and it runs on a separate track from the permit. Parkland is association country: Heron Bay, Parkland Golf & Country Club, Cypress Head, the MiraLago communities and most of the rest operate architectural review committees with their own packets, meeting calendars, contractor registration and work-hour rules. The city does not enforce private covenants, and your board does not issue permits. We build both approvals into one schedule so neither ambushes the other.

faqs.q: How long is a whole-house remodel from first call to move-back?
faqs.a: Design and engineering usually occupy a couple of months. Architectural review adds weeks depending on when the committee next meets, and city plan review adds more on top. Construction on a full interior gut commonly runs several months, longer once structure moves. The honest framing is seasons rather than weeks. We publish a written schedule alongside the estimate, then supervise daily to defend it instead of explaining it afterward.

faqs.q: What should a high-end remodel in Parkland cost?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on how much of the house genuinely changes, and anyone quoting a square-foot number before walking the property is guessing at your expense. A finish refresh and a gut that relocates plumbing, structure and mechanicals are different projects with different budgets. What we commit to is a scope written line by line with allowances tied to real selections, so the figure you sign is the figure you pay. We do not try to be the low number in a stack of three.

faqs.q: Do we have to move out while you work?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Parkland houses are large enough that phasing works more often than it does in smaller stock, and a two-story plan can let a family live upstairs while everything downstairs is open. Dust barriers, protected walking routes and a functioning kitchen somewhere are the minimum conditions. When the scope takes out every bathroom and the air handler in the same week, we say so early so you can arrange a rental rather than endure two bad months.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the floor plan and the running list of what annoys you. You get straight answers and a written, fixed-scope estimate, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Parkland, FL Kitchen Remodeling | PGX Builders Group
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Parkland kitchen remodeling that retires the builder layout: one wall out, a real island in, permits handled. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: The end of the builder kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Made-to-order cabinetry, slab stone, and the one structural opening that fixes a Parkland floor plan, permitted through the city, coordinated with your association, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The 2003 kitchen has served its time
intro_paragraphs: The Parkland kitchen problem has a date stamp on it. Houses built through the late nineties and the two-thousands in Cypress Head, Country Place, Parkland Isles and the earlier Heron Bay villages all shipped with the same plan: a corner sink under a small window, a peninsula standing in for an island, a desk nook that collects mail, and cabinets in whatever wood tone was selling that year. The square footage is already there. The layout never was. Kitchen remodeling at this level is mostly a matter of taking down one wall and rethinking both sides of it.

Once plumbing, electrical, mechanical and structure are in play, the kitchen gets permitted by the City of Parkland Building Department and inspected in stages, with plans filed through the city's online system as a signed and sealed set. Broward's amendments to the Florida Building Code apply on top of the state edition and are administered through the county Board of Rules and Appeals, and any new or enlarged window over the sink carries HVHZ product approval. One Parkland question worth settling early: if you want a professional gas range, find out whether your street has a gas main or your house would run on a propane tank.

There is an order that keeps a kitchen square, and we follow it. Cabinets are set first and stone is templated against what is actually installed, appliance models are confirmed before a filler strip is cut, and the cabinet order goes in at the front of the project because fabrication, not demolition, drives the calendar. Meanwhile the rest of the house stays sealed off, since a Parkland kitchen opens onto everything and dust travels the whole plan. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, permits pulled before anybody swings a hammer, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: Every part of the new kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Every kitchen is scoped line by line and priced before demolition. These are the moves that come up again and again in houses up here.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry to the ceiling
scope_items.desc: Custom boxes and doors finished for South Florida humidity and sized to nine and ten-foot ceilings, rather than stopping short and leaving a dust shelf.

scope_items.name: One wall, gone
scope_items.desc: Opening the wall between the kitchen and the formal dining room, with a sealed beam design and the new load carried properly down to footing.

scope_items.name: Islands that seat people
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain templated in place, over framing sized for a seating overhang instead of a cantilever supported by optimism.

scope_items.name: Appliances, finally relocated
scope_items.desc: Relocating range, hood, refrigeration and dishwasher, with venting, dedicated circuits and water lines run to code and signed off by an inspector.

scope_items.name: Power the house never had
scope_items.desc: Panel and service upgrades for induction cooking, double ovens and wine storage, none of which a 1998 electrical plan was drawn to support.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a kitchen renovation in Parkland?
faqs.a: Yes, unless you are only painting or sliding a new appliance into an existing hookup. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, changing venting or removing a wall all require permits from the Parkland Building Department, with inspections before anything is closed up. Minor maintenance below the city's small-repair threshold is exempt, but a genuine kitchen remodel is nowhere near that line. Unpermitted work reliably surfaces at resale, and correcting it later costs more than doing it once.

faqs.q: Will my HOA care about an interior kitchen?
faqs.a: Less than it cares about your elevation, but do not assume indifference. Associations in Heron Bay, Parkland Golf & Country Club and the MiraLago communities commonly regulate contractor registration, working hours, dumpster and portable toilet placement, parking and gate access, and a few want notice even for interior work. New venting through an exterior wall or roof is an exterior change and gets reviewed on its own. We read your covenants before the first delivery truck arrives.

faqs.q: How many months should I set aside for a custom kitchen?
faqs.a: Fabrication sets the pace, not demolition. A truly custom package is measured, drawn, built and finished over a matter of months, so the order goes in at the front of the project and demolition waits until the delivery date is real. On-site work then runs roughly two months for a clean layout and longer once a wall comes out or plumbing relocates. Stone is templated after cabinets are installed, which adds a window nobody should try to compress.

faqs.q: Can we get a real island in a house built with a peninsula?
faqs.a: Almost always, and it is the single change that transforms these floor plans. It normally means relocating the sink and dishwasher drain, which on a slab means cutting concrete, rerouting and re-pouring, and it often means the dining room wall comes out so the island has room to breathe. All of it is permittable and routine for a contractor who has done it. What it is not is a weekend of swapping cabinet doors.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen remodel run?
faqs.a: Selections drive this far more than square footage does, and cabinetry is usually the largest single line, with slab material and appliances behind it. Rather than float a range that means nothing, we walk the space, write a specification and attach a fixed price to it, so you are comparing something real. If price alone is going to decide this, we would rather learn that in the first meeting than the third, and we will say so plainly.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos or walk us through the kitchen in person. You will get a straight answer on layout and a fixed written price, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Parkland Bathroom Remodels, FL | PGX Builders Group
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Parkland bath renovations: garden tubs retired, curbless showers detailed to spec, well-water treatment handled. Estimates at (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs across Parkland, with flood-tested waterproofing, filtration where the house runs on well water, and every permit and inspection carried by a licensed, insured general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Well water, second floors and marble
intro_paragraphs: Bathrooms are where Parkland houses show their age first. The two-thousands primary suite arrived with a corner garden tub under a glass block window, a separate shower roughly the size of a phone booth, cultured marble tops and a toilet room behind a louvered door. Nobody has filled that tub since closing day. Owners in Terramar, Watercrest and Cypress Cay, and on the older Country Place and Cypress Head streets, keep commissioning the same renovation: the tub goes, the shower absorbs the space, and the vanity wall gets rebuilt around storage that actually holds something.

Bathroom work here is permitted through the Parkland Building Department, with separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections before anything gets covered, and that sequence is the entire point, since it is the only proof the rough plumbing and the waterproofing were right. Broward inspectors are certified through the county Board of Rules and Appeals and work from the Broward amendments layered onto the Florida Building Code. Out on the acreage in Pine Tree Estates and The Ranches there is an extra question, because those sections are not on city water and sewer. A private well and a septic system change what a bathroom project involves.

This is a small building with unforgiving tolerances, and we treat it that way. Shower pans get flooded and left overnight before anyone opens a box of tile, every slope is checked against a level rather than a feeling, and baths sitting above living space get pan detailing, pipe isolation and blocking that respect the ceiling below them. Slab work goes to installers who have done enough of it to be trusted with the last piece. The scope is fixed in writing, a supervisor is here every working day, and everything between your front door and the work gets covered first. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Powder room refresh or full primary suite rebuild, the scope is settled in writing before anything is ordered. The components below are the usual cast.

scope_items.name: The garden tub, retired
scope_items.desc: Removing the corner soaker nobody uses and reclaiming that footprint for a wet room, a genuinely wide shower, or the closet the suite always lacked.

scope_items.name: Showers detailed to spec
scope_items.desc: Bonded waterproofing, flood-tested pans, linear drains and low or zero-curb entries where framing allows, with heavy glass hung on real blocking.

scope_items.name: Second-floor protection
scope_items.desc: Pan assemblies, isolated supply lines and proper blocking for upstairs baths, because the ceiling below is where a shortcut announces itself first.

scope_items.name: Vanities and slab tops
scope_items.desc: Custom vanity cabinetry replacing cultured marble, with slab counters, undermount basins and lighting positioned for a face instead of the back of a head.

scope_items.name: Water treatment and venting
scope_items.desc: Filtration and softening for houses drawing from a private well, plus quiet exhaust ducted fully to the exterior rather than dumped into an attic.

faqs.q: I am on well water in Pine Tree Estates. Does that change a bathroom remodel?
faqs.a: It changes the specification more than the construction. Many properties in Pine Tree Estates and The Ranches sit outside city water and sewer and draw from a private well, and untreated South Florida groundwater is hard and frequently heavy in iron. It stains stone, spots glass and shortens the life of cartridges and finishes. We size filtration and softening into the scope and choose fixture finishes that tolerate the water, instead of letting you discover the problem in year two.

faqs.q: Can I add a bathroom if the house is on septic?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but the septic system decides that, not the floor plan. Adding fixtures or bedrooms increases the load an onsite system has to carry, and that gets permitted separately from your city building permit, through the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, which still runs onsite sewage permitting locally. The drainfield may need enlarging or replacing, and its footprint plus the required setbacks shape where new construction can go at all. On acreage lots we get the system evaluated before drawings are finalized.

faqs.q: Which parts of a bathroom renovation need a permit?
faqs.a: For anything past paint and a new mirror, yes. Replacing or relocating plumbing, altering circuits, adding an exhaust fan or changing the layout all require permits from the Parkland Building Department and inspections along the way. Cosmetic maintenance under the city's small-repair threshold does not. The inspection record is worth having for its own sake, since it documents that the pan and the rough plumbing were approved before tile hid them from view.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower on a slab?
faqs.a: Often. On the ground floor it means saw-cutting and recessing the slab, rerouting the drain and re-pouring, all of which is routine and all of which gets permitted. Upstairs we sink the pan into the framing instead. Where the structure genuinely refuses to cooperate, a low-profile curb with correct slope is the honest alternative, and you will hear which one your house supports before you commit to a photograph you saved.

faqs.q: What kind of budget does a primary suite bath take?
faqs.a: The visible half is stone, glass and fixtures. The invisible half is waterproofing, new supply and drain lines, ventilation and electrical, and that is the half people underestimate. A guest bath and a full primary suite rebuild are not remotely the same project. We would rather measure than guess, so the number arrives after a site visit and lands in writing against a named specification. We compete on finish quality and certainty.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Point at the bathroom you have been avoiding. We will scope it honestly and put a real number in writing, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions for Parkland, FL Homes | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Casitas, second stories, rear extensions and enclosure conversions in Parkland, FL, with zoning, tree and HOA review handled. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, guest houses and enclosure conversions on Parkland lots, engineered and permitted through the city, cleared with your architectural committee, and built under daily supervision.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing between the trees and the easements
intro_paragraphs: Parkland produces two kinds of addition, and they barely resemble one another. Out on the acreage in Pine Tree Estates and The Ranches, adding on means real space: a guest wing, a workshop, a cabana, an in-law suite that stands nearly on its own. Inside the platted communities like Parkland Isles, Cypress Head, Heron Bay and Parkland Golf & Country Club, the house is already generous and the lot is the binding constraint, so projects tend toward rear extensions, screen enclosures converted into conditioned rooms, and bonus space built over the garage.

Additions bring every review layer out at once. Zoning goes first, and the City of Parkland measures setbacks, lot coverage and height against its land development regulations long before anyone discusses beam sizes. The Building Department then reviews structure from a signed and sealed set, and the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals certifies the plans examiner and the inspectors who will sign it off. On lake and canal lots, drainage and maintenance easements across the rear quietly consume the yard you were counting on. Your architectural committee reviews massing, roof and materials on its own calendar, in parallel.

Additions are where twenty-plus years of South Florida building stops being a line on a website. Getting a new footing to behave as though it has always been attached to the old one, matching a stucco texture troweled fifteen years ago, blending roof tile the manufacturer discontinued: those details decide whether the work reads as original or as an afterthought. Keeping a family comfortable in the other half of the house while it happens is the rest of the skill. Scope fixed in writing before we break ground, a supervisor here every working day, one team through warranty.
home-additions.scope_heading: Where the extra square footage comes from
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition begins with an engineer and an honest read of the approvals ahead. These five cover most of what we build in this part of Broward.

scope_items.name: Extending into the yard
scope_items.desc: Family rooms, primary suites and kitchens pushed out into the yard on new footings, with tie-beams, framing and the roof connection detailed by an engineer.

scope_items.name: Screen cage to real room
scope_items.desc: Converting a screened patio into conditioned space with adequate foundation, impact openings, insulation and a mechanical extension, so the area counts at appraisal.

scope_items.name: Second story and bonus space
scope_items.desc: Building over the garage or adding a full upper floor once an engineer has evaluated the existing block walls, footings and truss layout honestly.

scope_items.name: Guest houses and casitas
scope_items.desc: Separate suites, cabanas and in-law quarters on acreage lots, sited around septic drainfields, well setbacks and the trees the city protects by ordinance.

scope_items.name: Garages and workshops
scope_items.desc: Detached or attached garage and shop buildings on the larger lots, engineered for wind load and finished to match the house rather than a barn.

faqs.q: What limits how big an addition can be on my lot?
faqs.a: Zoning does, long before structure enters the conversation. Parkland's land development regulations govern setbacks, maximum lot coverage and height for your district, and recorded easements trim the rest. Lakefront and canal-adjacent lots in the platted communities normally carry drainage or maintenance easements across the rear, and nothing gets built inside them. We pull the survey and the zoning numbers first, so design starts inside the envelope that actually exists rather than the one you hoped for.

faqs.q: How does HOA architectural review work on an addition?
faqs.a: It runs parallel to the city, and it is where the design questions actually get decided. Associations across Parkland review elevations, roof pitch and tile, stucco finish, window profiles and how the new volume reads from the street, and most meet on a fixed calendar rather than on demand. Several require the contractor to register and post insurance before gate access. Design for approval from the first sketch and it moves; fight the covenants and you buy another meeting cycle.

faqs.q: I am on septic. Can I still add on?
faqs.a: Usually, with planning. On the acreage in The Ranches and Pine Tree Estates, an addition that adds bedrooms or bathrooms increases the load on an onsite sewage system, and that gets permitted separately from the building permit, through the county health department rather than the city. The drainfield also occupies real land, and required separations from it and from the well restrict where a new footprint can legally land. We evaluate the system before an architect finishes drawings.

faqs.q: There are protected trees where I want to build. Now what?
faqs.a: Now you either design around them or you apply. Parkland requires a permit to remove, relocate or replace a tree or palm, and the city reviews those applications on its own timeline. Relocation is frequently approved where outright removal is not. The practical move is folding a tree survey into the site plan early, because a specimen in the wrong place is a design input, not a surprise at permitting.

faqs.q: Add on, or list the house and move?
faqs.a: For a lot of owners here, yes. The schools and the street are usually why they bought in the first place, and an addition buys exactly the space they are short while keeping the lot, the canopy and the address. Parkland lots frequently have room to work with. It is still major construction with zoning review, architectural review, permits and months of activity, so it rewards people staying put. We will tell you honestly whether the idea pencils before you pay an architect.

home-additions.cta_sub: Show us the survey and the idea. We will talk feasibility, approvals and honest numbers before anyone draws anything, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Backyards & Summer Kitchens, Parkland FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Outdoor living in Parkland, FL. Summer kitchens, covered terraces, pergolas and pool decks, engineered and permitted, tree rules included. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Parkland backyards deserve better than a slab
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered terraces, pergolas and pool decks for Parkland backyards, engineered for wind uplift, permitted through the Building Department, and built by a licensed general contractor who respects the tree ordinance.
intro_paragraphs: Parkland was named for what it looks like, and residents defend that on their own lots. Backyards here run large by South Florida standards, backing onto water in Heron Bay and MiraLago, onto preserve edges near the Doris Davis Forman Wilderness Preserve, or onto open acreage out in The Ranches. What owners commission is an outdoor room rather than a patio: a covered terrace with fans and shade that works in August, a summer kitchen with real utilities, a pool deck resurfaced in stone, and a screen enclosure that is not the aluminum cage the builder left behind.

Parkland's rules bite hardest outdoors, and the trees are the reason. The city requires a permit to remove, relocate or replace a tree or palm, applications go through the online permitting portal, and it is not a same-week approval. Structures, gas, water and electrical each need their own permits from the Building Department, and every new opening carries HVHZ product approval because Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. Then your association reviews the design, since a pergola visible from the lake path is unmistakably an exterior change.

We build outside to the standard we build inside. Footings for a pergola or pavilion get engineered for uplift, because a shade structure that leaves the ground in September was never worth building. The gas line and circuits feeding a summer kitchen carry their own permits and inspections, and grading gets settled on paper so water leaves the terrace instead of pooling at the threshold. Materials get specified for real exposure: stainless that survives, stone sealed on a schedule, cabinetry rated for weather rather than merely marketed for it. Fixed scope in writing, daily supervision, and a job site your neighbors have no reason to mention.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Resurfacing a pool deck or rebuilding an entire backyard, every element below is designed, permitted and constructed as one coordinated project.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens that work
scope_items.desc: Cooking, sink and refrigeration on permitted services, built in weather-rated cabinetry and stone rather than indoor materials moved outside and hoped for.

scope_items.name: Roofs over the terrace
scope_items.desc: Solid-roof extensions, pavilions and shade structures on engineered footings, uplift connections detailed, and the new roof tied into the existing line cleanly.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and driveways
scope_items.desc: Travertine, porcelain pavers and finished concrete over a properly prepared base, pitched to drain through a Parkland rainy season instead of ponding at the door.

scope_items.name: Screen enclosures, rebuilt
scope_items.desc: Replacing tired aluminum cages with current wind-rated framing and screen, or converting that footprint into a solid covered room where the permit path allows.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and glass
scope_items.desc: Exterior stucco repair, repainting within the association's approved palette, and sliders or French doors replaced with HVHZ-approved impact units.

faqs.q: Do I really need a permit to take down a tree in my own yard?
faqs.a: In Parkland, yes. The city requires a permit to remove, relocate or replace a tree or palm on private property, applications are submitted through the city's online permitting system, and how long review takes depends almost entirely on how complete the package is. Given what the city is named after, this is not treated as a formality. The common outcome is a footprint that shifts a few feet, or a tree that moves rather than disappears.

faqs.q: What approvals does a summer kitchen need?
faqs.a: More than the grill suggests. The structure needs a building permit, and the gas, plumbing and electrical each get their own permit and inspections through the Parkland Building Department. If it lives under a new covered structure, that structure gets engineered for wind. Your association reviews appearance separately, because it is an exterior change to a lot they oversee. The permit set, the association packet and the inspection calendar are all part of our job.

faqs.q: Can I convert my screen enclosure into a covered room?
faqs.a: Frequently, and it is one of the better returns available on a Parkland lot. The existing slab and footing have to be verified as adequate, the new roof gets engineered for uplift, and if the space will be air conditioned it needs insulation, impact-rated openings and a mechanical extension. In code terms that makes it an addition, so expect zoning review for lot coverage alongside architectural sign-off on how the new roof looks from outside.

faqs.q: Will an outdoor kitchen actually survive out here?
faqs.a: The right one will. Heat, humidity, sprinkler overspray and, on well-water lots, mineral-heavy irrigation are hard on everything left outdoors. We specify marine-grade or powder-coated stainless, dense stone that gets sealed on a schedule, weather-rated cabinet boxes and hardware chosen for the exposure. Big-box outdoor cabinetry photographs well for two seasons and then stops. Buy it right the first time and the terrace still looks like part of the house a decade later.

faqs.q: How disruptive is a backyard project day to day?
faqs.a: The yard belongs to the crew for a stretch, and there is no way around that. Expect material staging, a concrete day or two, and access routes planned so heavy equipment does not shred irrigation lines and sod on the way in. Most Parkland communities set construction hours and require contractor registration at the gate, and we work inside those rules. We sweep at the end of every day. Interior life continues more or less untouched.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Show us the yard and describe the evenings you want out of it. A written, fixed-scope estimate follows, in English o en español.

Broward then adds the county to the picture: its Board of Rules and Appeals maintains the local amendments layered onto the Florida Building Code, certifies the plans examiner who reads your set and the inspectors who sign it off, and issues the formal interpretations that end arguments. Every opening and roof assembly needs documentation valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. Taking down a tree needs its own permit.

Where a submittal needs an architect, an engineer or a surveyor, we retain one and coordinate the set. Review comments get answered once and completely, because a second and third round costs weeks. A supervisor meets the inspector on site. In twenty-plus years here and 150-plus remodels and additions, all permitted and inspected, the expensive problems we have watched owners inherit were rarely structural. They were filing failures, and they sat quietly until someone ran a title search.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: Permit work, before and after the fact
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Half of this gets filed before anything is built. The other half is cleanup, usually with a closing date on the calendar. Five jobs, either way.

scope_items.name: Open permits before a sale
scope_items.desc: We pull the full history on the address, work out exactly what each dormant record is still missing, and take it through inspection, revision or a replacement permit.

scope_items.name: Work that was never filed
scope_items.desc: Garage conversions, storm-rebuilt screen enclosures, summer kitchens and acreage outbuildings brought onto the record with as-built drawings, engineering where structure is involved, and an actual inspection.

scope_items.name: Approved products, matched anchors
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors, garage doors and roof assemblies go into review with approval documents matched to the design pressures on that wall, not a generic sheet from a brochure.

scope_items.name: Inspections called once
scope_items.desc: We request each phase when the work is genuinely ready and stand there while the inspector looks, because a failed call sets back every trade queued behind it.

scope_items.name: The approvals running alongside
scope_items.desc: Tree removal permits, your architectural committee packet, and the county reviews that attach to wells, septic systems and lake or drainage easements on the older acreage.

faqs.q: The title search turned up an open permit from 2007. What now?
faqs.a: First we read the file, because open is not a single condition. Some permits are missing only the final inspection nobody ever called. Some need a revision, or a sealed letter from the engineer of record. Some expired while the work sat half finished, and some cover work that was never permitted at all and now has to be legalized after the fact. Every one of those paths ends with an inspector looking at something, so the day you learn about it is the day to start.

faqs.q: Do I need a Broward County permit as well as a Parkland one?
faqs.a: For a house, no. Parkland reviews, issues and inspects its own residential permits, and the submittal goes up through the city's portal. The county Board of Rules and Appeals sits a level above that, maintaining the amendments your plans examiner applies and certifying the people who apply them, which is why a Broward inspection feels consistent from city to city. Where the county does turn up directly is out on the acreage: wells, septic systems and anything built inside a drainage easement.

faqs.q: My HOA approved the pergola. Is that the same as a permit?
faqs.a: No, and the two run on separate tracks. Architectural committees at Heron Bay, Parkland Golf & Country Club, Cypress Head and the MiraLago communities review how a thing looks and where it sits. The city reviews whether it stands up in a hurricane and whether the power and gas feeding it are safe. Neither substitutes for the other. The same applies to trees: Parkland requires a permit to remove, relocate or replace a tree or palm, and an architectural approval is not that permit.

faqs.q: Does my house need a milestone inspection or recertification?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. Florida's milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies apply to condominium and cooperative buildings three habitable stories and taller, and Parkland is a city of one and two family homes. Broward also requires periodic safety inspections for older buildings that are not one or two family dwellings, administered through the Board of Rules and Appeals. Where that reaches Parkland is your association: a clubhouse, a fitness building, a guardhouse. If your board just received a notice, that is a permitted repair project, and we build those.

faqs.q: What does permitting add to the schedule and the cost?
faqs.a: On the schedule, think weeks rather than days, and the first submittal sets the pace. A complete set draws one round of comments; a rushed one draws three, and each round restarts the clock. Structural work, a tree removal or anything touching an easement runs longer, because those reviews happen in sequence. The fees belong to the city and track the declared value of the work, not our margin. Closing out somebody else's old permit is the one thing nobody can price honestly before reading the file.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Open the file before the build
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address and the closing date, if you have one. You get the record read back plainly and a written scope to clear it, in English o en español.
